featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place has a G+2 seating arrangement—non-AC on the ground floor and AC seating on the first and second floors. Seating is decent.

Unlike many traditional bars, no complimentary chakna is served here. Alcohol prices felt on the higher side, and the 180 ml vodka was served from a larger container instead of a sealed bottle, which was a bit disappointing. Mixers were limited to Coke and Sprite only. Initially, staff said outside mixers would be charged extra, but after speaking to the manager, they allowed to buy it from outside without any charge.

Service was decent but not very attentive, especially towards regular or light drinkers—attention seemed more focused on heavy customers.

Coming to food: Apple Chicken was good, and the green kokani/malvani-style kairi chutney served with it was unique and delicious. We ordered Chicken Thali (₹300) and Mutton Thali (₹430). Quantity felt slightly less for the price—total four pieces (two gravy, two fry). Taste-wise, chicken and mutton gravies and fries had almost the same masala, which reduced variety.

Ambience is decent overall, but the washroom ceiling is quite low, which can be uncomfortable for tall people.

Overall, a decent experience—good chutney and some dishes stand out, but quantity, attention to service, and a few basic facilities can definitely improve.

featured_reviews.review_text: I came across this place through an influencer’s video and decided to visit for myself. We ordered the chicken thali, bangda thali, and solkadhi. featured_reviews.name: Rajesh Garvanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this restaurant mainly because the name included “Gomantak”, expecting decent seafood. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a huge disappointment.
We ordered pomfret fry, prawns masala, mushroom chilli, and roti. The waiting time was almost one hour, which was already frustrating. When the food finally arrived, the experience only got worse.
The pomfret fry was absolutely bland, with no salt or spices—completely tasteless and frankly pathetic. The prawns masala was just okay, nothing special and far from what you’d expect from a place claiming coastal flavors. Mushroom chilli and rotis were average at best.
Overall, a regretful visit. The food quality and taste did not justify the long wait or the expectations set by the restaurant’s name. Definitely not worth it and would not recommend.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Found this hidden gem in Marol and what an experience! Nav Gomantak brings the true coastal flavors right to Mumbai.

What I tried:
Bharlela Bombil (Chutney) - Absolutely stellar! The stuffed bombil was perfectly spiced and the chutney complemented it beautifully. A must-try!

Prawns Koliwada - Crispy, flavorful, and addictive. The coating was perfect and the prawns were fresh and juicy.

Kairiche Panha - Refreshing and authentic raw mango drink. Perfect to balance the spicy food!

Kokum Sarbat - Cool and tangy, exactly what you need with coastal food.

Pomfret Thali - Fresh fish, perfectly cooked with authentic Konkan-style preparation. The thali was wholesome and satisfying.

Chulivarcha Chicken - Traditional chulha-style preparation that brings out the smoky flavors. Outstanding!

Tandalachi Bhakri & Solkadhi - The perfect accompaniment to complete the coastal experience.

The food quality is top-notch, portions are generous, and the authenticity is unmatched. Service was prompt and courteous. If you're craving genuine Konkan cuisine without traveling to the coast, this is THE place!

Highly recommended for seafood lovers!!

Location: Easy to find in Marol, opposite CISL Police Camp
Value for money: Excellent!

Will definitely be coming back for more!!

featured_reviews.name: William Gonsalves
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sharing my honest and no filter review. Visited this place with my friend on Tuesday, 9th June after filtering Sai Palace out.
We went on a weekday and unfortunately the tandoor wasn't available from Monday to Friday. It was disheartening to hear tha bcz we wanted to order prawns tandoori. Now that we had already sat on the table we tried to run through the Food Menu. I asked the server, for possible options in non veg starters since tandoor wasn't available and I was surprised to hear that Ghee roast is a starter item and not a main course. On asking the reason the server responded that at Nav Gomantak they treat it as starters. None the less we ordered Prawns Ghee Roast and Bombil Fry. Prawns were 80% cooked and bombil fry had no salt and taste. One word "pathetic". For main course we ordered Chulvarcha mutton and Jeera rice and i was surprised to hear Chulvarcha Mutton (mutton prepared on coal/wood fire) is prepared on gas they has just named it Chulvarcha. Again below average taste mostly over Burnt. Could taste the burnt masala rather than fried. We couldn't finish the mutton and hers rice and packed it and took it with us.
Next day my mother ate the mutton dish and she too said the same thing.
So the restaurant is over hyped. The food is no influence of malvani cuisine let alone Goan cuisine. Spent 2000 for the food, experience 3/10.
Fancy seats, bright lightings or good looking cutlery doesn't guarantee you good and VFM food is what Nav Gomantak taught us. Skipping this restaurant forever. Hope the owners read my comment and improve the food quality.
The 4.3 rating is just a scam

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Something’s Fishy last week to celebrate a family friend’s birthday.

If you’re a seafood lover, Something’s Fishy is the kind of place that instantly feels right. From the moment you step in, the ambience sets the mood. The interiors have a beautiful seafood-inspired theme, artistically done without being over the top. Subtle marine elements, thoughtful décor, and warm lighting make the space feel relaxed and inviting. It’s comfortable enough for a family dinner yet stylish enough for a special outing.

We tried quite a variety of dishes, and honestly, the experience from start to finish was satisfying.

Harra Channa ka Shorba (Chicken Soup): A comforting, mildly spiced chicken soup with fresh herb flavours. Light yet flavourful, it had a soothing warmth and well-balanced seasoning, perfect to begin the meal.

Chicken Gassi: Rich, coastal-style chicken curry with aromatic spices and creamy coconut base. The gravy was flavourful without being overpowering, and the chicken pieces were tender and well-cooked.

Appams: Soft, fluffy appams with delicate crisp edges. Light texture and subtle sweetness paired beautifully with the gassi gravies, soaking up flavours perfectly without becoming soggy.

Prawn Gassi: Fresh prawns cooked in traditional coastal gravy with coconut and spices. The prawns were juicy and tender, absorbing the rich masala while retaining their natural sweetness.

Butter Garlic Prawn: Perfectly sautéed prawns tossed in butter and garlic. Simple yet delicious, with a lovely aroma and balanced seasoning that allowed the freshness of the seafood to shine.

Surmai Fry: Crispy on the outside, moist and flaky inside. The fish was fresh, well-marinated, and fried just right, delivering bold coastal flavours without excessive oiliness.

Rawas Tandoori: Well-marinated rawas grilled to perfection in the tandoor. Smoky, juicy, and packed with spices, yet the fish remained soft and flavourful inside.

Squid Crispy Fried Rings: Lightly battered squid rings fried till crisp. Crunchy outside, tender inside, with balanced seasoning that made them addictive without feeling too heavy.

What stood out throughout the meal was the freshness of the seafood. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, not rushed. Portions were generous, and the flavours felt authentic rather than overly commercialised.

Service was smooth and friendly. The staff were attentive, happy to recommend dishes, and ensured everything was served at the right pace. They didn’t hover unnecessarily, which made the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, Something’s Fishy delivers exactly what you expect from a seafood speciality restaurant — fresh ingredients, authentic coastal flavours, and a warm, pleasant ambience. It’s definitely a place I’d revisit whenever seafood cravings strike. Highly recommended for anyone who truly enjoys well-prepared seafood.

We started with some refreshing drinks. The dragon fruit cooler and plum cooler were both well balanced and not overly sweet.

We tried several dishes and every one of them stood out:
•	Surmai Slice Tawa Fry – perfectly crispy and super fresh.
•	Crispy Shell Stuffed – crunchy outside, creamy inside. Absolutely delicious.
•	Crab Gassi with Neer Dosa – rich coastal gravy paired with soft neer dosa… the best combo of the night.
•	Lobster Chilly Garlic with Appam, Lobster Cilantro Kalwan, Lobster Lemon Sabayon – each one packed with flavour and cooked perfectly.

featured_reviews.name: Akshata Manjrekar
featured_reviews.review_text:

I tried the Crab Tandoori, which was smoky, tender and well-spiced, and the Lobster Goan Masala, which had rich coconuty flavours and authentic coastal masala — both truly delicious. Overall, a memorable and unique seafood dining experience that feels special and worth checking out before the festival ends.

Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

featured_reviews.name: The Lucky Guide
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was contemplating to either visit Stacks and Racks or Malhar Tribes, so after consulting my date, he recommended that I visit Malhar coz it's just a few hundred meters away from where I live.

I arrived & was greeted by a lady host who didn't seem very welcoming coz I was all by myself, chose the ac section and asked for a place to wash my hands, and when I stepped in, there was this girl who was throwing up in the washroom.

Browsed through the menu & ordered a B&W whiskey, bombil rawa fry, squid rings & as per the waiters suggestion ordered a crab meat butter garlic, since I did not want to deal with the crab shells.

The food items arrived, squids came in first, followed by the crab meat butter garlic and lastly the bombil rawa fry. Since I was the only person eating I tasted every item served at the table, loved the bombil, liked the squids, the crab meat was more like Continental style that I'm not very fond of. I was under the impression that the chef/cook would have their own style of the prep. That's where the one star was lost.

I ate how much I could, and wanted to eat maincourse as well so I was saving some place in my tummy. After asking for the menu for the second time and waiting for one of the waiting staff to come take my order, nobody arrived, even after keeping my appetizers plate aside, nobody cared, after telling the waiting staff that I'm waiting to eat lunch, nobody came. They were all busy serving the larger tables of course coz it could mean more revenue and more tips.

Nevertheless, when I realized that nobody was coming to take my maincourse order, I asked for the bill and that came in no time. I paid and I left.

So if I am choosing to spend 4k for a single person, the least I expect is some good service, which this place missed out on big time, probably they judged me and that's why the lack of service.

Overall the experience was ok, I loved the food though. Will it be on my visit again list, the answer is NO! Why? Due to the poor service.

featured_reviews.name: rosh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Malhar Tribes with a family group of 10 adults, and honestly, the experience didn’t come close to the hype.

Starters: Fish Fingers,bombil rawa fry, surmai tawa fry, French fries, and a cigar-style appetizer with a dip. The cigar starter was actually good, but the bombil and surmai were a letdown—bland, not juicy, and completely lacking flavour. Definitely not what you expect from seafood that’s supposed to shine.

Mains: we had prawns koliwada, pomfret gassi, prawns gassi, neer dosa, appam, jeera rice, along with a manchow soup. Again, everything was just average. Nothing was bad, but nothing stood out either—no depth, no punch, no reason to come back.

Service: this was another downside. It was quite slow, especially during mains when you expect things to move faster. We had to repeatedly look for waiters just to place or follow up on a single order. For a weekend rush, this felt poorly managed and took away from the overall experience.

Dessert: the gulab jamun at ₹230 didn’t even feel worth ₹23. That’s not just disappointing, that’s hard to justify. Chocolate brownie with Ice cream was fine.

The total bill came to around ₹16,000 for 10 people. Fair at a glance, but for the quality and overall experience, it feels overpriced. You expect much better at that price point.

Overall, it’s okay for a group outing, but if you’re going in expecting great food based on the reviews, this place will likely leave you underwhelmed.

The food was really good. We ordered a chicken starter along with the prawn curry rice and pork vindaloo. The prawn curry rice combo is a must try. Coming from Kerala it gave me those beach vibes. The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. Great food, great flavours! We went here for lunch on a Friday afternoon  - it was quite packed - recommend reservation.

We ordered: Bombil fry and Surmai for starters. Followed by Prawns Gassi, Rawas Pulimunchi with Neer dosa and Malabar paratha. I personally liked the curries with the neer dosa better. We finished off with kulfi and caramel custard for dessert.

Felt it was a bit pricey but overall enjoyed the meal a lot. As a quick feedback, I’d urge them to move away from blue lighting and install more yellow lights. :)

The food, service, and ambiance are all incredible. We had a perfect time—the dishes were delicious and the atmosphere is stunning and perfect for groups. Seriously, every corner is Insta worthy! Highly recommend for a fun night out with friends.

featured_reviews.name: SHIRLEY GAIKWAD
featured_reviews.review_text:
I wouldn’t recommend this place.
I visited after a long break, hoping for the same experience Mahesh was once known for, but it was extremely disappointing. The ghee roast tasted odd, and the masalas were clearly undercooked. I felt nauseous after eating it. The soups were bad too, they tasted burnt, and even after asking for a remake there was barely any improvement.
The restaurant is expensive, which wouldn’t be an issue if the food justified the price, but this was absolutely ridiculous.
The neer dosa was raw and felt like one dosa had been cut in half and served as two. The squid was just about bearable, but by then the overall experience had already ruined the meal.
We left feeling completely disappointed. What made it worse was that even after complaining to the manager, nothing was done to address our concerns.
Mahesh used to be much better. Sadly, that quality is gone now.
Please save your money and skip this place.

The flavours were perfectly balanced, the food was served hot, and everything tasted extremely fresh. Service was smooth and made the entire experience even better.A must-visit place for seafood lovers. Truly authentic, fresh, and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Sheetal Upadhyay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent Experience at Nav Chaitanya, Andheri West ⭐️
Nav Chaitanya in Andheri West is a gem for anyone who loves authentic, homely food. The moment you step in, you get a simple and welcoming vibe that makes you feel comfortable and relaxed. It’s a great place for family meals as well as casual outings.
🍽️ Food:
The food is absolutely delicious and full of authentic flavours. The seafood dishes are especially outstanding — fresh, well-cooked, and perfectly spiced. The thalis are filling and satisfying, with generous portions that truly feel value for money. Every dish tastes fresh and home-style, which is what makes this place special.
👨‍🍳 Service & Ambience:
The staff is polite, attentive, and quick to help. Service is smooth even when the place is busy. The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable — letting the food do all the talking.
💯 Overall:
Nav Chaitanya is a must-visit for anyone looking for authentic coastal and Maharashtrian flavours in Andheri West. Great food, good service, and a comforting dining experience. Highly recommended for seafood lovers and family dining!

featured_reviews.name: Raghav Kukreti
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a first time traveller in Mumbai, I didn't know any good restaurants, went here because it was recommended by friends and what can I say other than it's honestly the best seafood I've had in my life.

I've already gone again in 2 days and plan to go again before leaving. The fish is extremely fresh; as a newcomer I told the server that I didn't know what to order except I knew I wanted to eat tandoori crab. They were extremely helpful, kept checking in if everything was okay and the service was a 10/10.

I ate tandoori crab and a pomfret thali the first day. Crab was 10/10 spicy very flavorful and they were helpful enough to break the claws. The pomfret was succulent, flaky, no offensive flavors. Even my wife who is mostly vegetarian ate the fish like she's been eating it for years. A huge testament to this restaurant.

The second time we ate Bangda and Rawas thalis. Both were amazing. The bangda fish was so good we ended up ordering a second order of 2 bangda frys. Another 10/10.

Had modak as dessert which was also soft, juicy and just lovely. The kokam soda is also the best way to cleanse your palate.

In closing I would like to say, if you have any desire to eat seafood, this place is a blind go. You cannot go wrong with anything you order. 100/10.

Machali rani is a take away restaurant located at khar west , Mumbai. We ordered the following,
1) Bharit pomfret ( stuffed pomfret): pomfret stuffed with a green chutney. We enjoyed this albeit the size of the fish was a little small .
2) Surmai fry: the fish was fresh and consisted of two pieces of surmai
3) Bombil fry: fresh and very well fried.
4) Prawns curry: tad oily for my liking but tasty.
All the dishes had fresh fish and was tasty. Will definitely order again. Highly recommended.
They are available on Zomato and swiggy only but if you have a bulk /party order you can call the number available online.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Small, but Neat & Clean Airconditioned Restaurant with just a Handful of Tables located next to the popular Gulati Sweets on the main Mahakali Caves Road in Andheri East, that Specializes in Authentic Malvani Seafood and offers a Wide Range of Thalis.
The Menu is quite extensive, the Fish is Fresh, the Preparations are Authentic Malvani Cuisine, the Service is Prompt and the rates are Very Reasonable too. Since the Rates are a bit low, the quantity of Fish served is a bit less, but good enough for an average eater.
Parking is on the Main Road which is always busy and can be a Challenge, as there is no Valet Parking. While there is a Wash Basin to Wash your hands, there is no Washroom available.
A good place to go to for enjoying a Variety of Fresh Seafood Prepared in Authentic Malvani Masalas and at Very Reasonable Rates too.

featured_reviews.name: Kaivan Doctor
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a very popular Malavni & Kokani cuisine  restaurant  in Lalbaug area.
It is popular for its fresh seafood,Mutton & chicken dishes.
It follows thali system.
Ambiance  is simple & ethnic,comfortable seating,fully air-conditioned . There are two restaurants with different decor but same menu separated bya spectacle shop.
Service is friendly,but sometimes can be very slow as restaurant is full most of the time.Waiters are well dressed & courteous.
Restaurant is very clean & follows good hygiene.
Their menu has a few seafood,Mutton & chicken starters.
Then different varieties  of thalis.
We had specially gone there to have good fresh seafood but found the rates too high as they were as per size.
A Surmai orpomfret thali at around 1000/- however big the fish sounds too high so we had to skip them.
We had a Prawn thali which was tasty with vade & had fried prawns not very big,prawn masala,fish curry,sol kadi,vade & rice for 550/- which was good & tasty.
Also had a Mutton thali with vade for 550/- which was also tasty & worth the price having mutton masala,mutton masala ,sol kadi,vade,rice.
On the whole it was a good meal except for the high pricing of fish items. No rice dishes like biryanis are available  on the menu which is also disappointing.
Can visit with family when in lalbaug area.

featured_reviews.review_text: The food was excellent and fresh fish was served. Their speciality is thali & authentic malvani food. You may have to wait little longer for service. featured_reviews.name: Pooja Uday Parulekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
You should visit Majghar only if you’re genuinely hungry because the portions here are massive! The food is absolutely delicious and satisfying. It’s not exactly pure Malvani or Konkani cuisine, but more of a fusion with Vidarbha-style flavors, which actually makes it stand out. Every dish has a homely yet rich taste that leaves you wanting to try more.
The atmosphere is lively and comfortable perfect for families or groups. The interiors have a simple, rustic charm and the overall vibe makes you feel right at home. What really impressed me was the staff they’re extremely polite, attentive, and always ready to suggest the best dishes based on your taste.
Overall, Majghar is a place that balances great taste, generous portions, and warm service beautifully. Highly recommended if you love traditional Maharashtrian flavours and don’t mind rolling out full and happy!

Bold claim.

Ordered Surmai, Pomfret and Prawns.
Pomfret actually lived up to the promise — fresh and tasty.
Surmai felt like it had already celebrated a day or two, and the prawns didn’t exactly scream freshness either.

Fish is seasonal. Not everything shows up fresh every day — a little honesty would’ve helped choose better.

Prices are already premium, and then GST plus a surprise 5% staff welfare charge joins the party on the bill.

Good kitchen, but transparency could be much fresher.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 – Authentic Malvani Taste at Its Best!

Visited Malvani Klub Restaurant at Lalbaugh with my wife, and we were genuinely impressed with the food, service, and overall experience. We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

The Bangda fry in the thali had that perfect Malvani masala flavour, and the curries were rich, aromatic, and truly reminded us of homely Maharashtrian coastal food. The prawns curry was equally flavourful, and the chapatis were soft and fresh.

Apart from the excellent food, the staff deserves a special mention — very polite, friendly, and attentive. They made the dining experience even better with their warm hospitality.

If you love Maharashtrian or Malvani cuisine, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Group of 4. Saturday Dinner. Mid April 2026.

Having visited countless seafood restaurants across Goa, the Konkan region, and Mumbai, I can confidently say that Jai Hind tops my list.

Yes, there’s almost always a long waiting line, and at times you may be asked to share a table with other diners. But honestly, that’s only because the place is packed with people who keep coming back for the food. And once you taste it, you’ll understand why.

The seafood is fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. What makes the experience even better is the value for money. Unlike many places that charge extra for every little thing, the thali here is genuinely generous and unlimited, you can ask for refills of the items in your thali as many times as you’d like.

Great food, excellent portions, and prices that feel justified. If you’re a seafood lover, the wait is absolutely worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Niv Shetye
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mast Malvani – A Hidden Gem in Lalbaug for True Malvani Flavours
📍 Located near Currey Road, Lalbaug, Mumbai

If you’re in search of authentic Malvani cuisine in Mumbai, you’ll know that many places fall short when it comes to delivering real flavors. But hidden in the heart of Lalbaug lies Mast Malvani, a modest eatery that truly lives up to its name. With over 2000+ reviews and a solid 4.3 rating, we decided to finally give it a try—and we’re glad we did!

---

Ambience & Experience

The restaurant is small, with just about 5 tables, seating around 30-40 guests at a time. Despite the size, their management is top-notch. We were given a wait time but seated within 15 minutes. What’s smart? They take your order while you wait, so your food hits the table almost as soon as you sit down. Efficient, right?

---

What We Ordered

🐟 Surmai Thali

A generous piece of Surmai Fish—choose between Rava Fry or Green Masala Fry (both were phenomenal, each with its own distinct coastal kick).

Served with Konkani-style fish curry, Javla (dry shrimp), Solkadi, your choice of Bhakri / Wade / Amboli, and rice.

Every bite screamed authentic Malvani coastal soul food.

🍗 Chicken Thali

One bowl of rich and spicy Malvani Chicken Masala

Another bowl of comforting Malvani chicken gravy

Accompanied with Bhakri, Solkadi, and a signature Malvan-style chutney that stole the show.

The spice, flavor, and balance were spot on.

---

Must-Try: Solkadi

We've had Solkadi across Mumbai, but this one? Truly refreshing, authentic, and soothing. You’ll want seconds.

---

Final Verdict

Whether you're craving a satisfying thali or want to go à la carte, Mast Malvani delivers on all fronts — taste, speed, hospitality, and affordability. It’s no-frills but full-on flavor.

💰 Super pocket-friendly
⭐ Perfect for solo meals, family dinners, or food trails
📍 If you’re around Lalbaug, Currey Road, or even just nearby — don’t miss this spot.

Mast Malvani is not just another Malvani restaurant. It’s THE Malvani restaurant you’ve been looking for in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Karaday
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hidden away in the heart of Lalbaugh lies a true culinary treasure - Mast Malvani! This unassuming eatery is a haven for lovers of authentic Marathi Malvani cuisine. Upon my recent visit, I was treated to an exceptional experience that has left an indelible mark on my taste buds.

The star of the show was undoubtedly the Chicken Tikka Biryani. Each morsel of succulent chicken was infused with a symphony of spices that danced on my palate. The rice was perfectly cooked, and the fragrant biryani masala elevated the dish to a whole new level. This biryani is a must-try for any biryani aficionado.

The Wade at Mast Malvani are a revelation. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, they were served piping hot and accompanied by an array of chutneys that complemented them beautifully. The balance of flavors and textures was impeccable, showcasing the chef's mastery in the kitchen.

The Chicken Tikka was another highlight. The pieces were marinated to perfection, resulting in tender, juicy bites bursting with smoky flavor. It's evident that the chefs at Mast Malvani take great care in ensuring the quality and taste of each dish.

The restaurant itself exudes a charming, cozy ambiance. While it may be a small space, it is impeccably clean and exudes a warm, welcoming atmosphere. The staff were attentive and eager to share their knowledge of the dishes, adding a personal touch to the dining experience.

In addition to the culinary delights, the prices at Mast Malvani are refreshingly reasonable, making it accessible to a wide range of diners. For the quality of food and service provided, it's an absolute steal.

All in all, Mast Malvani is a hidden gem that deserves to be discovered by food enthusiasts far and wide. Whether you're a fan of Malvani cuisine or simply looking to embark on a gastronomic adventure, this establishment is a must-visit. Be prepared to be swept away by the flavors, and don't miss out on their Chicken Tikka Biryani, Wade, and Chicken Tikka - they're absolute show-stoppers!
